open_points.subject: source_folder.read_named_source result
open_points.text:
- deciding whether a requested name passes condition 1 of A3 rule 5, and reading that file once without
  following a link;
open_points.question: What exact result crosses from source_folder to photo_delivery, who owns that result type, and how does it distinguish condition 1's NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT from each A1 order 1-to-6 rejection while also carrying the bytes and file metadata?
options: A tagged source_folder result containing bytes, modification time, and a condition/rejection code
Typed source_folder exceptions that photo_delivery maps to PlacementFailure
A result expressed directly in PlacementFailure members, coupling source_folder to the placement model
open_points.default_guess: Give source_folder ownership of a tagged read result and let photo_delivery map its tags to PlacementFailure.

open_points.subject: read_named_source path race
open_points.text:
- deciding whether a requested name passes condition 1 of A3 rule 5, and reading that file once without
  following a link;
open_points.question: Must the opened file be reached through the same non-symbolic path components whose metadata passed condition 1, including when an untrusted folder component is replaced between the metadata checks and the open, or does no-follow apply only to the final component?
options: Anchor traversal with directory descriptors and refuse if any component changes into a symbolic link
Check path metadata first and use a final-component no-follow open
Recheck the path after opening and accept the opened file if the recheck passes
open_points.default_guess: Use descriptor-relative traversal that never follows any component and treat a race detected during opening as UNREADABLE_FILE.

witness.initial: The requested name is sub/photo.jpg; sub is a real directory and photo.jpg has the requested source_id when condition 1 reads the path metadata.
events: Syncthing-fork replaces sub with a symbolic link to a different directory after the metadata check and before source_folder opens the file.
The calling flow asks to deliver sub/photo.jpg with a source_id matching the file reachable through the replacement link.
outcomes: A descriptor-anchored implementation refuses the open and no placement is made.
A final-component-only no-follow implementation reads through the replaced parent link and places the reachable image.
witness.observer: The calling flow observes failure versus placement, and the Portal binary store contains an image only in the second outcome.

open_points.subject: modification time associated with a named read
open_points.text: - the modification time of a file in the service's time form.
open_points.question: Which observation supplies the modification time returned with a requested read when the name is replaced between path-metadata validation and opening: metadata read through the name, metadata of the opened file descriptor, or a later metadata reading?
options: Use the opened file descriptor's modification time captured once
Use the path metadata captured for condition 1
Read the path metadata again after reading the bytes
open_points.default_guess: Capture the modification time from the opened file descriptor so it describes the same file object as the bytes.

witness.initial: photo.jpg has no usable camera date; inode A at that name has modification time T1, while inode B has modification time T2 and bytes whose hash is the requested source_id.
events: source_folder reads the path metadata while the name denotes inode A.
Syncthing-fork replaces the name with inode B before the open.
source_folder opens and reads inode B, and photo_preparation falls back to the supplied modification time.
outcomes: Using the earlier path metadata produces publication photo_date T1 for inode B's bytes.
Using the opened descriptor's metadata produces publication photo_date T2 for inode B's bytes.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different photo_date in the publication body.
